newsitem.title: UK: RTZ-CRA to take $40 mln reorganisation hit.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA to take $40 mln reorganisation hit.

text.p: RTZ-CRA, the international mining group said on Wednesday that it would take a one-off charge of $40 million to cover the costs of reorganising its management structure into six global product businesses.
Executive chairman Robert Wilson told a news conference that the reorganisation would result in annual cost savings of $50 million to $60 million before tax by 1998.
Wilson said savings would come from the closure of offices, including Kennecott Corp's Salt Lake City, Utah, office and the loss of 200 jobs worldwide.
The chairman said the goal of the restructuring was to achieve "a simple, flat structure" for management.

"RTZ-CRA is a big company by the standards of this industry. Most competitors concentrate on a single commodity. We are striving to obtain benefits of scale without the bureaucracy that goes very often with size," said Wilson.
Wilson said the Australian government had been approached before the shake-up was announced.
The changes did not undermine RTZ-CRA's dual structure as a British/Australian company, he noted.
News of the reorganisation has provoked an angry response in the Australian press.
